subject: SlateCommerce: Implementation orchestration for embeddings + rerank
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Jenna Park <jenna@slatecommerce.com>, Tom Liu <tom@slatecommerce.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SlateCommerce: kickstart - embeddings / rerank onboarding ops

Team —

Following up from the commercial close last week. SlateCommerce is ready to start onboarding for embeddings + rerank. High-level asks from the customer call: index backfill strategy that avoids impacting their search traffic, clear vector DB choice (managed vs self-hosted), and an acceptance plan for rerank that includes sample queries + manual eval.

Attached is an initial index spec (mvp_index_spec.xlsx) with current corpus sizes. Key facts:
- Catalog + product descriptions: ~18M docs (mostly short descriptions)
- User search logs (1Y): ~120M rows (we will sample for rerank eval)
- SLA: 99.9% availability target after cutover

Immediate ask: Marcus / Monica — can you draft an operational plan with (a) backfill wave schedule with throughput targets, (b) recommended vector DB and sizing rationale, and (c) rerank eval plan (sample size, metrics, roll criteria)?

I dropped a HubSpot link and the Drive folder with the raw export below.

Thanks — I can intro to their infra if you want a sync.

--
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mvp_index_spec.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Jenna Park <jenna@slatecommerce.com>, Tom Liu <tom@slatecommerce.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SlateCommerce: kickstart - embeddings / rerank onboarding ops

Thanks Aditya — looping in the implementation leads. Monica, Ben: high level plan I propose below; please flag anything missing. Jenna / Tom, copied so you can see the proposed cadence.

1) Wave strategy (backfills)
  - Wave 0 (canary): 100k docs, internal test tenant, validate index schema + vector dims, run smoke queries (48h)
  - Wave 1: product catalog (18M) split into 6 slices by vendor region, backfill at 400k docs/hr per slice during midnight maintenance window (2–5 AM PT)
  - Wave 2: supplements (pricing history + attributes) smaller slices at 200k/hr, 2 weekend waves for final sync
  - Wave 3: search log priming (sampled 5% of logs) for rerank model priming and priming thresholds

2) Vector DB recommendation
  - Recommendation: Managed vector store on Redwood Dedicated (Redis Enterprise for low-latency KNN), fallback to Pinecone managed for initial cutover for simpler ops. Rationale: low tail-latency, integration with Redwood prefix caching, and predictable throughput. Milvus/self-hosted favored only if customer requires on-prem.

3) Rerank eval plan
  - Sample: 3k queries uniformly sampled by query frequency + 500 long-tail queries (edge cases)
  - Metrics: NDCG@10, MRR@5, 7-point human relevance agreement for manual evals
  - Roll criteria: >= 5% improvement in business-mapped CTR or no degradations in top-1 precision, and manual pass on a 200-query blind set

Next steps: Monica — can you create a JIRA epic with the waves and assign owners? Ben — can you lead vector DB sizing and cost estimate? Jenna / Tom — does the nightly maintenance window above work for your ops team?

—Marcus
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: rerank-eval-sample.csv]

Nice plan. A few clarifying questions from the CSM side before I build the epic:

- Backfill impact: do we have an estimate for peak CPU/GPU and network egress per 400k docs/hr target? I want to confirm we won't trample their search cluster during the maintenance window.
- Vector DB failover: if we do managed Redis and it degrades, what's our automated fallback path? Can we auto-route to a lower-cost dense index (approximate search) to preserve latency?
- Rerank human eval: who will recruit raters? We typically do a mix of the customer's merch team + Redwood raters for edge cases. Need to lock names and NDA before we export logs for evaluation.

Proposed acceptance milestone timeline (tentative):
- Week 0: Canaries and smoke tests
- Week 2: Catalog cutover (Wave 1) with live shadow traffic for 72 hours
- Week 4: Full index complete + rerank A/B test for 2 weeks

I'll draft the JIRA epic if you confirm the compute profile and fallback plan.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-embed-operator-checklist.md]

On Wed, Sep 1, 2027 at 11:02 AM Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Jenna Park <jenna@slatecommerce.com>

Cc: Tom Liu <tom@slatecommerce.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SlateCommerce: kickstart - embeddings / rerank onboarding ops

Appreciate the clear plan. A few notes from our infra/security side:

- Maintenance window: Midnight–3AM PT is fine for the bulk backfills, but we need a 30-minute blackout buffer at the start and end for cache priming.
- Vector DB: We prefer a managed option but must have an encryption-at-rest guarantee and KMS integration (AWS KMS). Can you confirm Redwood Dedicated's KMS options?
- Rerank evals: we'll provide a list of 8 merch analysts to join the human relevance panel. We'll need a simple UI or CSV-based workflow for labeling.

We'll need the JIRA epic and a doc with explicit rollback steps before Wave 1. Looking forward to the JIRA.

—Jenna
Head of Search, SlateCommerce
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@slatecommerce.com>, Tom Liu <tom@slatecommerce.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SlateCommerce: kickstart - embeddings / rerank onboarding ops

Jenna — thanks for the confirmations. Quick updates and attachments attached:

- KMS: Redwood Dedicated supports AWS KMS; I'll include the integration steps in the implementation checklist.
- Blackout buffer: we will schedule a 30-minute buffer pre/post each nightly slice; ops will run a health check and cache warm before we flip traffic.
- Rerank labeling: Monica — we'll provide a CSV export + a minimal labeling UI (internal) to accelerate the 8 merch analysts. Ben, please size the labeling VM and set up the secure S3 bucket for exports.

I've attached the operator checklist and a sample rerank eval CSV with suggested sample buckets. I'll also create the JIRA epic tonight and link here (HubSpot deal updated).

Next sync: Monday 09/06 10:00 AM PT for sprint kickoff unless you prefer otherwise.

Thanks all —
Marcus Lin
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redwood-embed-operator-checklist.md, rerank-eval-sample.csv]
